elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience,” in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Termination requires thirty days’ prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vendor must refund prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the termination effective date, which provides a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid Fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered language requires only thirty days’ notice, not 60 to 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee applies; the clause expressly permits termination without penalty or early-termination fee, which is more protective than a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly denied any convenience-termination right during a term; no broader Vendor convenience-termination right is granted.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, so the triggering condition for a Vendor notice obligation is demonstrably absent.
